method: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Peel and cut the potatoes into even 2cm chunks. Boil for 15–20 minutes until a knife goes through easily, then drain and mash with 2–3 tablespoons of the hot cooking water; no milk or butter is added.
Dice the carrots finely. Stir together the measured light mayonnaise, wholegrain mustard, black pepper in a small bowl and keep this dressing chilled until serving.

Heat half the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan. Cut the lean pork loin into even 2cm pieces. Fry over medium-high heat for about 8–12 minutes, turning regularly. Cook until no pink remains inside and the pieces are steaming hot throughout; a clean thermometer should read 75°C for 30 seconds at the centre. Transfer the cooked filling to a clean plate.

Add the remaining measured olive oil, carrots and 60ml water to the pan. Cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the carrots soften; add the peas for the final 3 minutes and cook until piping hot. Add a spoonful of water if the pan dries before the carrots are tender.
Return the cooked filling to the vegetables. Keep the chilled dressing separate for serving; spoon the hot filling into a small ovenproof dish.

Spread the mashed potato over the filling and roughen the top with a fork. Bake for 15–20 minutes, until the top colours and the centre of the pie is steaming hot. Rest for 2 minutes. Serve the light mayonnaise, wholegrain mustard, black pepper dressing alongside.
